title: Method for microplastics extraction from Lake sediments
author: Zobkov, Zobkova, et al.

steps.title: Preliminary wet peroxide oxidation
steps.instruction: Weigh 400 g of wet sediment into an 800 mL glass beaker, add 20 artificial reference particles (ARPs), then add 50 mL of 30 % H₂O₂ in 15–25 mL portions while stirring with a glass rod; control the reaction, transfer any overflow to another beaker, and cover the beaker with aluminum foil once the reaction finishes.

steps.title: Sediment flushing through filter cascade
steps.instruction: Set a blank sample, add 100 mL distilled water to the beaker and mix, then pass the slurry through a three‑stage filter‑funnel cascade (meshes 333 µm, 174 µm, 100 µm). Wash each net with distilled water until only solid remains, collecting the drain in a discard beaker. If a net clogs, scrape the retained sediment into an 800 mL beaker, cover with foil, and replace the net. Repeat until the entire sample is transferred, rinse the original beaker, and check for ARP loss with a UV lamp. Dispense 300 mL potassium formate solution (ρ = 1.5 g mL⁻¹) into a 500 mL cylinder, wash the nets with this solution, and pour the remaining solution into the beaker containing the sediment.

steps.title: Density separation
steps.instruction: Stir the mixture of sediment and potassium formate for several minutes, cover with foil, and let it settle for 2–5 days. Examine the floating layer for ARPs and record their abundance. Number two 10 × 10 cm filter nets (F1, F2) with 174 µm mesh, place them in a two‑stage funnel cascade, and filter the solution through them. If any ARPs remain below the surface, add more potassium formate, stir, and let settle for 24 h; repeat until all ARPs are recovered. Rinse F1 and F2 with distilled water to remove residual potassium formate. The potassium formate solution can be vacuum‑filtered (174 µm net + 3–5 µm cellulose filter) and reused if its density remains ≥ 1.5 g mL⁻¹.

steps.title: Wet peroxide oxidation with Fenton’s reagent
steps.instruction: Transfer filter nets F1 and F2 into an 800 mL beaker, add 25 mL of 0.05 M Fe(II) solution and 25 mL of 30 % H₂O₂, cover with foil and let stand for 5 min at room temperature. Place the beaker in a water bath at 70 °C, monitoring for vigorous boiling; add distilled water with a squirt bottle if overflow occurs. If organic matter is still visible, add another 25 mL of 30 % H₂O₂ and repeat until digestion is complete. Cool for 2–5 min, then add 25 mL of 4.5 % HCl to dissolve chitin and mineral residues.

steps.title: Filtering and drying of control nets
steps.instruction: Remove F1 and F2 with tweezers, wash with distilled water, roll into cones, and dry at room temperature in a desiccator covered with sieve cloth; place each dried net in a labeled Petri dish (CONTROL 1). Filter the remaining solution through a second two‑stage cascade of 174 µm nets (F3, F4), rinse the beaker to transfer all solids to F3/F4, wash the nets, and if no optional density separation is needed, roll and dry them as above, labeling the dishes PRIMARY.

steps.title: Optional density separation (sand removal)
steps.instruction: If sand is present, invert F3 and F4 over the density separator, wash with 100 mL potassium formate, cover, and let settle for 1 h. Roll F3/F4, wash with distilled water, dry, and label as CONTROL 2. Discard the settled fraction. Set a new two‑stage cascade, transfer the floated material to two fresh 174 µm nets (F5, F6), wash the separator with potassium formate, roll F5/F6, wash with distilled water, dry, and label the dishes PRIMARY.

steps.title: Internal quality control (blanks)
steps.instruction: For every five samples run one blank: place a clean 174 µm round net (B1) in a Petri dish, keep it moist during the filtration step, then process it through the same oxidation, washing, and drying steps as samples, labeling it BLANK CONTROL. After oxidation, filter the remaining solution through two 174 µm nets (B2, B3), dry them, and label them PRIMARY BLANK.

steps.title: Microscopic identification of microplastics
steps.instruction: Record sample, filter‑net and workstation details in the workbook. Fix each filter net on lined cardboard with paper clips, use tweezers and a dental probe to separate items, and identify MPs according to Norén criteria (no cellular structure, uniform thickness for fibers, clean color). Classify each item as fiber, fragment, film or bead, assign it to one of thirteen color groups, and measure its size (length for fibers; length × width for others) with the microscope scale. Note the number of ARPs recovered on F1. For chemical confirmation, place a ~1 mm drop of distilled water on an object plate, transfer the item with tweezers, cover with a cover glass, fix with scotch tape, pack in foil, label the specimen, and register it.

steps.title: Calculation of microplastic abundance
steps.instruction: Sum MP counts by color and type on all relevant filter nets (CONTROL 1, CONTROL 2 if performed, PRIMARY, and PRIMARY BLANK) using the formulas provided for Ncolor,type, Nblankcolor,type, and NBCcolor,type (set to zero if negative). Aggregate NBC values to obtain Ntype for each shape, then total Nsample. Compute abundance A = Nsample × 100 % / (msample × (100 − W)), where msample is the dry sediment mass (kg) and W is the sample wetness (%).
